successors.note: "In 1285 Ali b. Wali Asma deposed the kings of Shewa and installed a certain MHz"; Shewa became one of the seven districts of Ifat.

capitals.name: Walale
capitals.note: "Its capital Walale was situated in northern Hararghe in Harla country" (also Walalah, Welela as the former capital). The page gives no coordinate: Dire Dawa, in the same part of northern Hararghe, is used as a stand-in.

correction.text: the Sultanate of Showa, capital Walale in northern Hararghe

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Sultanate). "Its territory extended possibly to areas west of the Awash River"; no area on the page. Only northern Hararghe is drawn; the possible western reach (the Shewa plateau, region 'Shewa') is not.

ledger.note: 896: the Sultanate of Shewa is established. "Shewa Sultanate, established in 896, is the first Muslim state inland"; "This ruling house governed the polity from AH 283/AD 896 to 1285-86"; Amir Haboba is the earliest documented ruler (896-928). The page names Walale in northern Hararghe, not a border.

ledger.note: 1285: Ifat conquers Shewa. "In 1285 Ali b. Wali Asma deposed the kings of Shewa and installed a certain MHz"; Ifat's ruler "Wali Asma deposed Shewan kings and established the Walasma dynasty". The infobox gives 1279 as the last year; the body says 1285-86.

wars.note: The Ifat dossier (af-01-b) cites the infobox "Shewa conquered by Ifat: 1278-1285". The Showa page names conflict with Damot as a main cause of decline (Mohammed Hassen).

sources.title: Kingdom of Damot
sources.note: Infobox c. 10th/13th century to c. 1316; location south of the Abay; capital Maldarede; tribute from Shewa in the 13th century; conquest by Amda Seyon in 1316/7.

notes: New dossier: Cliopatria lacks the Sultanate of Showa. Pages opened: Sultanate of Showa, Kingdom of Damot (2). The ifat-sultanate dossier (af-01-b) already uses counterpart 'sultanate-of-shewa' and region Harar (region) for its 1285 gain; this dossier agrees. Disagreements: the infobox last year 1279 against the body's 1285-86 (taken); the capital Walale is placed in northern Hararghe, so the sultanate of 'Shewa' lay east, not in the Shewa plateau, which the page notes only as a possible extension west of the Awash. Ruler list: only Amir Haboba (896-928) is dated; the page says there were nine recorded sultans. The tribute to Damot is recorded in the kingdom-of-damot dossier. Capital coordinate is a stand-in (Dire Dawa). Gazetteer names needed: Walale (Walalah, northern Hararghe, Harla country).
